tasks.title: Label lane v2: M3 vision for outlined-text firms + callout-vs-room filtering
tasks.notes: Caught live on Harborview demo: outlined-text firms get zero labels (PDFTron sees 0 readable text). Spike run_labels_m3tiles.py proven at ~4.3 min/sheet. Needs MINIMAX_AI key on VPS and callout-vs-room filtering.

prep.what: Build an opt-in AI label-reading action for outlined-text firms using MiniMax M3 vision tiles, and add a callout-vs-room filter to suppress false matches (stair arrows, FEC callouts, general-note paragraphs).
prep.understand: PDFTron outlines ALL text on certain firms — the Harborview demo showed 55 live words extracted but zero room labels, because the text is rendered as vector paths, not live glyphs. The M3 tiles spike (`run_labels_m3tiles.py`) tiles the sheet, sends each tile to MiniMax vision, and reads labels visually. It works but costs money (metered §7a event) and takes ~4.3 min/sheet. Holabird proves the noise problem too: UP stair arrows, FEC callouts, and general-note paragraphs all match as 'room names' without a filter.
approach: Read `docs/spike/run_labels_m3tiles.py` — understand the tiling strategy, MiniMax call shape, and how labels come back (coordinates + text).
Add a POST `/sheets/{id}/labels/ai` service route that enqueues the M3 tiles lane as an RQ job with SSE progress, gated behind a metered-credits §7a event check.
Wire the `MINIMAX_AI` key to the VPS `.env` at `/opt/takeoff-engine/.env` (same placement pattern as other API keys) and smoke-test inference end-to-end through the prod service.

Build a callout-vs-room classifier: suppress matches that are all-caps multi-word paragraphs, contain directional keywords (UP, DN, FEC, ELEV, STAIR), or have bounding-box aspect ratios inconsistent with a compact room label (wide/short = note block).
resources: docs/spike/run_labels_m3tiles.py (proven tiling + MiniMax vision lane)
engine/labels.py (existing live-text lane for comparison)
PRD §7a metered-credits event spec
VPS .env at /opt/takeoff-engine/.env (API key placement)
Harborview and Holabird test sheets (outlined-text and noise examples)

tasks.title: Assemblies-per-room → paint/drywall/flooring quantities + wall heights
tasks.notes: `assemblies-lite` already scaffolded in engine/assemblies.py from B1. Full version: room_type → assembly formulas + heights (up to 8 quantities per room, CSI libraries). Last pillar before estimator-grade Excel.

prep.what: Build the full assembly engine: given a classified room (bedroom, bathroom, corridor…), compute all finishable quantities — wall SF, ceiling SF, floor SF, and linear feet of base trim — using CSI formulas and the room's actual perimeter and wall height.
prep.understand: `engine/assemblies.py` has a scaffolded `assemblies_lite` from Phase 2 (B1) that emits basic area lines. The full version maps `room_type` → a set of `(quantity_name, formula, unit, csi_code)` entries. `wall_height_ft` is already patchable on the service (Phase A PATCH route). Perimeter is in `meta.perimeter`. The output feeds into `engine/excel.py`'s 5-tab workbook — this is what transforms the Excel from a room-count sheet into an actual estimator tool.
approach: Open `engine/assemblies.py` — read `assemblies_lite` fully, understand the room dict it receives (classification, sf, perimeter, rings, wall_height_ft).

Design the room_type → assembly mapping: bedroom/living = walls + ceiling + floor + base trim; bathroom = walls + ceiling + floor (tile) + base trim; corridor = walls + ceiling + floor; open-plan = ceiling + floor (no base trim). Write it as a pure data dict.
Implement `full_assemblies(room: dict) -> list[dict]` returning `{name, qty, unit, csi_code}` — keep it pure and testable with no service imports.

Wire the new function into `engine/excel.py` so each room row in the workbook includes the assembly quantity columns; add 2–3 `pytest` cases for a known classification (e.g. bedroom at 9 ft, 40 LF perimeter → wall_sf=360, ceiling_sf=floor_sf, base_lf=40).
resources: engine/assemblies.py (existing `assemblies_lite` scaffolding)
engine/excel.py (5-tab workbook builder — wire output here)

tasks.title: Derive wall PAINT area (perimeter × height) — the missing painting measurement
tasks.notes: 2D plan has no height → painting gets ZERO auto-sqft from the takeoff engine. Add wall_height_ft to estimates; seeder must preserve geometry/perimeter (currently drops it). Wall paint SF/room = perimeter × height.

prep.what: Make painting estimates actually work from a blueprint: add a wall-height input to the takeoff flow and derive wall paint SF per room as `perimeter × height`, fixing the core gap in CT Pros's main trade.
prep.understand: Rafa's core business is painting but every takeoff import today seeds ZERO wall area — the 2D blueprint has no Z axis, and the seeder discards `geometry.rings` and `meta.perimeter` anyway. The engine already returns both in the measurement response. `wall_height_ft` already exists as a PATCH route on the takeoff engine (Phase A, t28). The seeder at `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php` is where geometry is dropped and where the fix must land. The result feeds directly into t46 (trade routing) and t48 (pricing) downstream.
approach: Write and run a migration adding `wall_height_ft` (float, nullable, default 9.0) to the `estimates` table; wire it through `EstimateController` and the `Takeoff/Index.vue` page as a user-editable project-level default.
In `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php`, preserve `geometry` and `meta.perimeter` from the engine's measurement response object — find where they're currently dropped and stop discarding them.

For each room measurement with a valid `meta.perimeter` and a non-null `wall_height_ft`, compute `wall_paint_area = perimeter × height` and emit it as a seeded line: `kind='painting'`, `unit='sqft'`, with the appropriate surface label.
Upload a real sheet to staging (e.g. CT Pros sample from the tester guide) and verify: a 12×14 room at 9 ft should produce ~936 sqft of wall paint area as a separate estimate line.

tasks.title: Route takeoff measurements to trades at the seam
tasks.notes: Every measurement collapses to one anonymous kind=custom $0 line — kind+geometry dropped. Switch on kind: area(SF)→flooring, derived-wall-SF→painting, line(LF)→wall-linear/trim, count(EA)→doors/tile.

prep.what: Route each engine measurement to its correct trade in the estimate (flooring, painting, trim, doors) instead of collapsing everything into a single anonymous $0 custom line.
prep.understand: The takeoff engine returns measurements with a `kind` field: `area` = floor SF, `line` = linear footage (trim, walls), `count` = unit count (doors, fixtures). Currently `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php` ignores `kind` and emits one `kind=custom` $0 line per room. The `ProjectType::isCoreTrade()` helper from t36 already classifies painting/flooring as self-perform and trim/tile as subcontracted. This task is the routing bridge that makes imported takeoffs meaningful — each measurement kind maps to the right `LineItemFactory` method and trade.
approach: Read `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php` seeding loop in full — locate exactly where `kind` is ignored and measurements collapse to a single line.

Write a `routeMeasurement(array $measurement, float $wallHeight): EstimateLineItem` method with a `match` on `$measurement['kind']`: `area` → `fromMaterial` with flooring rate + floor SF; derived-wall-SF (from t45 output) → painting rate; `line` → `fromLaborRate` with PerLinearFt trim rate (t47 prerequisite); `count` → door/fixture count line.
Use `ProjectType::group()` to set `is_subcontracted = true` on trim and tile lines (Rafa subs those out), and `subcontractor_id = null` (unassigned until Rafa picks the sub).
Test with a real CT Pros sheet on staging: confirm the resulting estimate shows distinct flooring, painting, and trim line items with correct units and non-zero areas.
resources: TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php (the seeding loop — find and fix the measurement collapse)
app/Enums/ProjectType.php (`isCoreTrade()` and `group()` from t36)
LineItemFactory.php (`fromMaterial`, `fromLaborRate`, `fromSubcontract` — pick the right one per kind)
Engine API measurement response — check `kind` field values in a real `GET /projects/{id}/measurements` response

tasks.title: Add PerLinearFt RateType (prerequisite for pricing trim/wall-linear)
tasks.notes: RateType has no per-linear-foot. Add PerLinearFt='per_linear_ft' + label, wire unitFromRateType->'lf', seed a per-LF trim LaborRate. Must land before t48.

prep.what: Add a per-linear-foot rate type to the RateType enum and seed a trim labor rate, so linear-foot measurements from the engine can be priced instead of landing at $0.
prep.understand: A 30-minute prerequisite for the full trade-routing chain. `RateType` drives how `LineItemFactory::unitFromRateType()` labels units and how `seedLabor()` looks up rates. Without `PerLinearFt`, any LF trim line from t46 has no pricing path and will be emitted as an unpriced stub. One enum value + one factory case + one seeder row.
approach: Add `PerLinearFt = 'per_linear_ft'` to `app/Enums/RateType.php` with a human label `'Per Linear Foot'`.
Add the `'per_linear_ft' => 'lf'` case to `LineItemFactory::unitFromRateType()`.
Add a trim `LaborRate` row in `LaborRateSeeder.php`: trade=`'trim'`, rate_type=`PerLinearFt`, rate=`4.50`, crew_type=`'subcontractor'` (Rafa subs trim).
Run `php artisan db:seed --class=LaborRateSeeder` on staging, then verify the new rate appears in the labor rates settings page.
